newsitem.title: FRANCE: French water utility blames state for pollution.
newsitem.headline: French water utility blames state for pollution.

text.p: French water utility Lyonnaise des Eaux said on Thursday it wanted the courts to force the state to share the blame for polluted water it was delivering to customers.

The utility said it would ask an administrative court in the western city of Rennes to shift much of the blame to the state for the condition of the water delivered to the town of Guingamp, which is polluted with nitrates.
Company officials said they wanted five million francs ($900,000) from the state to cover the damage done to its reputation by past findings that it was furnishing polluted water.

"The state has a responsibility for the management shortcomings that have contributed to the pollution of the water by nitrates," customer service director Jean-Luc Trancart told a news conference in Rennes.

Company officials blamed the high nitrate levels in the water used by the 20,000 people of Guingamp on fertiliser and chicken droppings from poultry farms, both of which are washed into local rivers by rainfall.
The utility was ordered in 1995 to pay 1,000 to 1,200 francs ($180 to $216) to each of 176 customers in the area who had formally complained of excessive nitrate levels in their water.
The company said it was required to spend 700,000 francs ($125,000) a year to purify the water in the area.
The 1995 ruling was the first in France to blame a utility for polluted drinking water.
